1. β– THALASSEMIA

-70,000 – affected worldwide.
-100 million – carrier worldwide.
-1000 in UK are affected.

Thalassemia Major requiring:

requiring > 7 transfusions/year.

Thalassemia Intermedia:

7 or less/ or no of transfusions.

Thalassemia is Diagnosed @ 2 – 7years.

Growth & development Abnormalities without Transfusion.

Corner stone of management => blood transfusion and chelation therapy.

Complications of Iron overload:

•Subfertility – hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
•Hypothyroidism.
•DM – damage to islet cells of pancreas
•Cardiomyopathy – cardiac failure 50% cause of death.
•Liver damage.
•Osteoporosis (ca+ chelation with chelating agents).

Pre conception counselling:

•High dose folic Acid (all women).
•Adequate chelation prior to Ovulation induction or conception.
•All hormonal contraception – safe.

MDT:

→Obstetrician – all women.
→Cardiologist – if cardiac problem.
→Hematologist – all women.
→Diabetologist if DM.
→Infertility specialist.
→endocrinologist – if endocrinopathy.
•OI with Gonadotrophins – if infertility – success of OI is more with good chelation.
•Optimum Glycemic control – fructosamine <300nml/l – at least 3m0 prior to conception.

Fructosamine 300nml/l = HbA1C 43mmol/mol.

•Optimize TFT’S – (if hypothyroidism).
•Optimize cardiac function: (all women)
→Consult Cardiologist.
→ECG.
→Echo.
→T2 – MRI.

- Target >20ms

- >20ms minimal Iron.

- <10ms – high load, risk of cardiac failure.

T2 – MRI < 10ms + EF => C/I to pregnancy.

-Hematologist, medicine specialist.

ANC:

•Monthly antenatal visits till 28 weeks, 2 weekly later.
•Routine as well as specialist care.
•DM – Monthly Fructosamine + specialist diabetic review.
•Cardiac assessment @ 28 weeks – all women with Echo:
-MRI => in pts wo have not received Pre conception assessment.
•Hypothyroid – TFT – periodically.
•USG:
→7 – 9 weeks for fetal viability as they have risk of miscarriage.
→Booking /dating @11 – 14 weeks.
→Anomaly@ 18 – 21 weeks.
→Serial Biometry 4 weekly from 24 weeks (IUGR).
•Transfusion in thalassemia major

Generally, transfusion regimen remains stable

target HB 100g/l. (pre – Transfusion).

Transfusion in thalassemia intermedia

Transfusion if:

→Worsening anemia
→IUGR
→Target Hb = same as non-pregnant
→Normal growth and low Hb => Formulated plan of transfusion
→Hb check every 2 – 3 weeks.
•Thromboprophylaxis:
•Splenectomy OR Plt >600 xO9 => Aspirin 75s.
•Splenectomy + Plt >600 xO9 => Aspirin + LMWH.
•Hospital Admission – LMWH.
•Delivery by SVD – LMWH during admission + 7 days after discharge.
•Cs – LMWH 6 weeks after birth

Iron Chelation During Pregnancy.
